# EggPdf

> Pure C# HTML/CSS-to-PDF rendering engine for .NET. Zero external dependencies. MIT license. Chrome-quality output.

Built by Eggspot. Open source: https://github.com/eggspot/EggPdf

## What it does

Converts HTML + CSS to PDF entirely in managed C#. No WebKit, no Chromium, no native binaries, no NuGet dependencies. Works on any platform where .NET runs (.NET Framework 4.6.2+, .NET Core, .NET 5–10).

## Install

```bash
dotnet add package EggPdf
```

## Quickest usage

```csharp
using EggPdf;

byte[] pdf = await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync("<h1>Hello World</h1>");
File.WriteAllBytes("output.pdf", pdf);
```

## Core API

```csharp
using EggPdf;

// Static one-liner
byte[] pdf = await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync(html);

// Configurable converter (reuse instance for performance)
var converter = new HtmlToPdfConverter(new PdfOptions
{
    PageSize = PageSize.A4,
    Orientation = PageOrientation.Portrait,
    Margins = new PageMargins(top: 20, right: 15, bottom: 20, left: 15, unit: Unit.Mm),
    DefaultFont = "Arial",
    Title = "My Document"
});

byte[] pdf = await converter.RenderAsync(html);
await converter.RenderToFileAsync(html, "output.pdf");
await converter.RenderAsync(html, outputStream, cancellationToken);
```

## PdfOptions reference

```csharp
new PdfOptions
{
    // Page
    PageSize = PageSize.A4,           // A4, Letter, Legal, A3, A5, ...
    Orientation = PageOrientation.Portrait,
    Margins = new PageMargins(20, 15, 20, 15, Unit.Mm),

    // Document metadata
    Title = "My Document",
    Author = "Jane Smith",
    Subject = "Monthly Report",

    // Typography
    DefaultFont = "Arial",            // Falls back to system fonts
    DefaultFontSize = 12,

    // Headers and footers
    Header = new HeaderFooter { Left = "{{title}}", Right = "{{date}}" },
    Footer = new HeaderFooter { Center = "Page {{page}} of {{pages}}", FontSize = 8 },

    // PDF conformance
    PdfVersion = PdfVersion.Pdf17,
    PdfA = PdfALevel.Pdf2b,           // Archival (1b, 2b, 3b)
    Tagged = true,                    // PDF/UA accessibility

    // Security
    Encryption = new PdfEncryption
    {
        UserPassword = "open123",
        OwnerPassword = "owner456",
        AllowPrinting = true,
        AllowCopying = false
    },

    // Output
    Compression = true,
    WatermarkText = "DRAFT"
}
```

## ASP.NET Core integration

```bash
dotnet add package EggPdf.AspNetCore
```

```csharp
// Program.cs
builder.Services.AddEggPdf(options => {
    options.PageSize = PageSize.A4;
    options.DefaultFont = "Arial";
});

// Controller action
[HttpGet("invoice/{id}/pdf")]
public async Task<IActionResult> GetInvoice(int id)
{
    var html = await RenderViewAsync("Invoice", await GetInvoiceAsync(id));
    return new PdfResult(html) { FileName = $"invoice-{id}.pdf" };
}
```

## Razor template integration

```bash
dotnet add package EggPdf.Razor
```

```csharp
builder.Services.AddEggPdfRazor();

public class ReportService(IRazorToPdfConverter pdf)
{
    public Task<byte[]> GenerateAsync(ReportModel model)
        => pdf.RenderViewAsync("Reports/Monthly", model);
}
```

## REST API (Docker / any language)

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 eggspot/eggpdf:latest
```

```bash
# Render HTML to PDF
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/render \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"html": "<h1>Hello</h1>", "options": {"pageSize": "A4"}}' \
  -o output.pdf

# Health check
curl http://localhost:8080/health

# Web UI
open http://localhost:8080
```

## CLI (standalone binary, no .NET needed)

```bash
# Download from https://github.com/eggspot/EggPdf/releases/latest
./eggpdf input.html -o output.pdf
./eggpdf input.html -o output.pdf --page-size A4 --margin 2cm
./eggpdf input.html -o thumb.png --format png --dpi 150
echo "<h1>Hello</h1>" | ./eggpdf - -o output.pdf

# Or install as dotnet tool
dotnet tool install -g dotnet-eggpdf
```

## Target frameworks

netstandard2.0, netstandard2.1, net6.0, net8.0, net9.0, net10.0

## Performance

- Simple page (h1 + p): **13 µs**, 20 KB
- Invoice (table + styles): **86 µs**, 85 KB
- Large table (100 rows): **1.2 ms**, 939 KB
- Thread-safe: reuse one `HtmlToPdfConverter` instance per application
- Streaming output: constant memory for large documents

## Key features

- Full HTML5 (WHATWG spec)
- CSS 2.1 + Flexbox (incl. auto margins, align-items:baseline), Grid, Multi-column, Custom Properties
- @media print, @page rules
- Webfonts: remote <link> stylesheets (Google Fonts) and @font-face over http(s)/data:/file, weight-accurate faces 300–900
- Full Unicode text: Vietnamese and extended Latin, per-codepoint symbol-font fallback (⚠ ✔ …)
- Browser-parity text layout: real font metrics for measurement, baseline placement, letter-spacing, word-break:break-all
- SVG (vector, not rasterized)
- Image formats: JPEG, PNG (incl. 1/2/4-bit grayscale QR codes), GIF, WebP, BMP, Base64
- Bookmarks, links, TOC
- Repeating table headers
- TrueType/OpenType embedding with subsetting
- Digital signatures: one-call X.509 signing (detached CMS/PKCS#7, adbe.pkcs7.detached) or external-CMS two-step flow
- Encryption: RC4 40/128-bit with owner/user passwords and permission flags — one-call `HtmlToPdf.Render(html, new PdfEncryption {...})` or REST /api/encrypt; all streams and strings encrypted per the PDF 1.7 Standard security handler
- Cloudflare email obfuscation (data-cfemail) decoded automatically
- PDF merging

## Security: signing and encryption

```csharp
using EggPdf;
using EggPdf.Pdf;
using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates;

// One-call PKI signing — embeds a detached CMS/PKCS#7 signature
// (adbe.pkcs7.detached) with a valid /ByteRange. Zero extra packages.
byte[] pdf = await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync(html);
byte[] signed = PdfSigner.Sign(pdf, x509CertificateWithPrivateKey,
    new PdfSigner.SignOptions { Name = "Jane Smith", Reason = "Approval", Location = "Hanoi" });

// Two-step flow when the private key lives elsewhere (HSM, signing service):
byte[] withPlaceholder = PdfSigner.AddSignaturePlaceholder(pdf, options);
// ... compute CMS bytes externally over the ByteRange content ...
byte[] done = PdfSigner.SignWithCmsData(withPlaceholder, cmsBytes);
```

View-only protection (RC4 40/128-bit, owner/user passwords, permission flags —
printing/copying/modifying). One call in code:

```csharp
byte[] protectedPdf = HtmlToPdf.Render(html, new PdfEncryption
{
    OwnerPassword = "secret",     // full access
    UserPassword = "",            // empty = opens without a prompt, permissions still apply
    AllowPrinting = true,
    AllowCopying = false,
    AllowModifying = false,
});
```

Or through the REST service:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/encrypt \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"html":"<h1>Confidential</h1>","ownerPassword":"secret","allowCopying":false,"allowModifying":false}' \
  -o protected.pdf
```

Note: PDF permission flags are advisory (enforced by compliant viewers, not
cryptography). For tamper evidence, prefer digital signatures — any change to
a signed PDF invalidates the signature.

## Architecture

8-stage pipeline: HTML Parse → CSS Parse → Style Resolve → Box Generate → Layout → Fragment → Paint → PDF Write
